_readme: Every text the RoboGuard phone app shows. One entry per text: change "text" and the app shows the new wording after the next start — no code change.
"note" says where the text appears and is never shown to anyone.
Placeholders are written in curly braces, e.g. "Drive to {location}"; the app fills them in. Keep them in the wording, otherwise that piece of information disappears.
Keys are read by the code; do not rename them. A missing key shows the key name on screen (visible instead of an empty label).
To change language, translate the "text" values here. Internal values (sleep durations, sensor names) are NOT texts and stay as they are.

meta.note: Reserved for settings that belong to the texts themselves.

app.header.title.note: Blue header at the top of the settings screen.

button.ok.note: Closes an information or error dialog.

button.cancel.note: Closes a dialog without doing anything.

pair.instructions.text: You need to scan the QR Code on your robot to pair your device.
pair.instructions.note: Big text on the pairing screen, before any robot is paired.

pair.button.scan.note: Button at the bottom of the pairing screen; opens the camera.

pair.error.title.text: Oops something went wrong when pairing with your robot!
pair.error.title.note: Dialog headline when the handshake with the robot failed.

pair.error.text.text: Please try scanning the QR Code again.

pair.qr.valid.text: Successfully scanned QR Code! Attempting to pair with robot!
pair.qr.valid.note: Shown right after a QR code was read and looks valid.

pair.qr.invalid.text: Please try to scan again! QR Code could not be verified.
pair.qr.invalid.note: Shown when the scanned code is not a RoboGuard pairing code.

pair.camera_permission.note: Shown instead of the camera when the camera permission was refused.

settings.category.sensors.note: Headline of the sensor section (camera, microphone, …), tap to fold out.

settings.category.situational.note: Headline of the situational section (discretion mode, pixelate objects).

settings.category.expand.note: Spoken description of the arrow of a folded section (screen readers only).

settings.category.collapse.note: Spoken description of the arrow of an open section (screen readers only).

settings.sleep.label.note: Row in the sleep section, in front of the chosen duration.

settings.info.discretion.title.note: Headline of the information dialog for discretion mode.

settings.info.discretion.text.text: The robot turns away automatically when it detects sensitive situations or nudity to protect your privacy.
settings.info.discretion.text.note: Explanation of discretion mode; shown when its name is tapped.

settings.info.pixelate.title.note: Headline of the information dialog for pixelating objects.

settings.info.pixelate.text.text: When enabled, the robot's camera stream will automatically blur objects or persons marked as private.
settings.info.pixelate.text.note: Explanation of object pixelation; shown when its name is tapped.

settings.info.unknown.text.text: Specific information for {setting} is not available.
settings.info.unknown.text.note: Fallback explanation for a setting the app has no text for ({setting} = its name from the robot).

settings.button.navigation.note: Green button that opens the robot's map screen on the phone.

settings.button.uncouple.note: Red button: forgets this robot, back to the pairing screen.

settings.button.sync.note: Sends the privacy settings to the robot.

sync.success.title.note: Dialog headline after the robot accepted the settings.

sync.success.text.text: Your privacy settings were successfully saved on your robot
sync.success.text.note: Dialog text after a successful save.

sync.failed.title.note: Dialog headline when the settings could not be sent.

sync.failed.text.text: Could not connect to the robot. Please check your connection.
sync.failed.text.note: Dialog text when the robot could not be reached.

sync.reload.title.note: Dialog headline when the robot now offers other sensors or rooms.

sync.reload.text.text: The robot's available sensors or rooms have changed. The UI will now be updated.

sync.reload.button.note: Button that reloads the screen with the robot's new configuration.

sleep.dialog.title.note: Headline of the dialog that picks how long the robot sleeps.

sleep.option.none.note: Sleep choice: the robot does not sleep.

sleep.custom.title.note: Headline over the three fields for a freely typed duration.

nav.header.title.note: Header of the map screen on the phone.

nav.button.back.note: Leaves the map screen. The robot keeps driving.

nav.switch.debug.note: Switch at the bottom: shows the status lines and the robot's log.

nav.state.connected.note: Next to the green dot: the robot is answering.

nav.state.connecting.note: Next to the grey dot: the first answer is still on its way.

nav.state.offline.note: Next to the red dot: the robot server was not found.

nav.state.refused.note: Next to the orange dot: the robot answered but refused.

nav.banner.offline.text:
The robot server was not found ({reason}).
Check that the phone is in the same WiFi as the robot and that the robot is switched on. Showing the last known state, {seconds}s old.
nav.banner.offline.note: Red banner while the robot cannot be reached ({reason} = technical cause, {seconds} = age of the shown state).

nav.banner.refused.note: Red banner when the robot answered with an error ({code} = HTTP code, {extra} = explanation below, {reason} = the robot's wording).

nav.banner.refused.unpaired.text: The pairing with this robot is no longer valid; pair again.
nav.banner.refused.unpaired.note: Added to the banner above when the robot no longer knows this phone (401). Starts with a space.

nav.button.retry.note: Button in the red banner: try to reach the robot again now.

nav.warning.not_running.text: The navigation is not running on the robot: {reason}
nav.warning.not_running.note: Shown when the robot answers but its navigation is not started.

nav.label.unknown_reason.note: Used when the robot gives no reason.

nav.button.drive_to_none.note: Same button while nothing is selected (it is switched off then).

nav.button.stop.note: Red button: stops the drive at once.

nav.label.speed.note: Headline over the three speed buttons.

nav.speed.default.note: Speed choice: whatever the robot uses by itself.

nav.label.places.note: Headline over the list of places.

nav.label.no_places.note: Shown when the robot's map has no places.

nav.label.place.note: One entry of the place list ({x}/{y} = coordinates in metres).

nav.button.save_position.note: Saves where the robot stands right now as a named place.

nav.button.clear_points.note: Removes the points tapped on the map; named places stay.

nav.button.reload_map.note: Makes the robot read its map and places again.

nav.button.delete.note: Deletes the selected place, or a private area.

nav.label.areas.note: Headline over the list of private areas.

nav.label.no_areas.text: No private areas on this map.
nav.label.no_areas.note: Shown when no area is marked private.

nav.label.areas_not_loaded.text: Not loaded yet — the robot refuses to drive until they are.
nav.label.areas_not_loaded.note: Shown while the robot has not read its private areas (it does not drive then, on purpose).

nav.label.area_allowed.note: Under an area the robot may currently cross ({time} = minutes:seconds).

nav.button.revoke.note: Ends a temporary permission to cross an area right now.

nav.button.area_circle.note: Marks a circle around the selected place as private.

nav.button.draw_area.note: Starts drawing a private area on the map.

nav.button.undo.note: Removes the last corner while drawing.

nav.button.finish_area.note: Closes the drawn area ({corners} = number of corners so far).

nav.hint.drawing.text: Tap the map to add corners of the area.
nav.hint.drawing.note: Hint while an area is being drawn.

nav.map.none.note: Placeholder while the map picture has not arrived.

nav.map.description.note: Spoken description of the map picture (screen readers only).

nav.label.map.note: Debug line: which map the robot uses.

nav.label.localized.note: Debug line: does the robot know where it is, and may it use the robot system.

nav.label.navigation.note: Debug line: what the robot is doing right now.

nav.label.position.note: Debug line: where the robot stands, in metres.

nav.label.unknown.note: Answer in the debug lines when the robot did not say.

nav.label.remote.note: Shown while a phone is steering the robot ({client} = its name).

nav.error.areas_unreadable.text: Private areas could not be read: {error}
nav.error.areas_unreadable.note: The robot cannot read its saved private areas; it refuses to drive then.

nav.error.locations_unreadable.text: Saved places could not be read: {error}
nav.error.locations_unreadable.note: The robot cannot read its saved places.

nav.button.show_log.note: Shows the robot's own event log.

nav.dialog.crossing.title.note: The robot asks whether it may cross a private area ({area} = its name).

nav.dialog.crossing.text.text: The robot's way goes through this private area. Yes allows it for {minutes} minutes.
nav.dialog.crossing.text.note: Text of that question; {minutes} = the chosen duration.

nav.button.yes.note: Green: allows crossing for the chosen minutes.

nav.button.no.note: Red: the robot stays out of the area.

nav.dialog.name.position.note: Headline when a place is being named.

nav.dialog.name.area.note: Headline when a circular private area is being named.

nav.dialog.name.drawn_area.note: Headline when a drawn private area is being named.

nav.dialog.message.title.note: Headline of the dialog that shows the robot's answer to a command.

nav.message.unreachable.text: The robot could not be reached: {reason}
nav.message.unreachable.note: Shown when a command did not arrive.

nav.message.refused.note: Shown when the robot refused a command without its own wording.
